content:
natalie: Hey team, escalated from ACME - streaming responses over SSE are truncating on reconnects and customer is seeing partial output + duplicate billing. Repro steps and logs attached below. :worried:

natalie: Summary: client opens SSE, receives partial token stream, client reconnects (backoff) and eventually receives the remainder, but sometimes the server replays a previous chunk leading to duplicated tokens and charge counts. Happens in both node-sdk 1.7.2 and python-sdk 0.9.0.

natalie: Observed behaviour:
- initial stream: emits tokens up to "...order confirmed" then client disconnects (network).
- on reconnect, server resumes but emits last n tokens again, client concatenates -> duplicate text.
- billing shows two partial invoice entries for same request id.

natalie: Logs from customer (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T16:12:02Z] SSE open id=abc123 session=customer-A
[2026-03-15T16:12:04Z] event=token data="Order"
[2026-03-15T16:12:05Z] event=token data=" confirmed"
[2026-03-15T16:12:06Z] connection lost (ECONNRESET)
[2026-03-15T16:12:08Z] reconnect attempt #1
[2026-03-15T16:12:09Z] event=token data=" confirmed"  <-- duplicate replay
[2026-03-15T16:12:09Z] event=end request_id=req-789
```

natalie: Repro snippet customer used (Node):
```js
// naive reconnect logic
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } });
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log(e.data);
es.onerror = () => setTimeout(() => new EventSource(url), 500);
```

natalie: Python client used similar iterator pattern that yields tokens into a buffer and resumes on reconnect.

ryan: Can you paste the exact request payload (model, stream flags, resume_token if any) and the SDK versions + HTTP proxy info? also any rate-limit headers we returned?

natalie: Model: "redwood/gpt-1.3b", streaming=true, no explicit resume_token in payload. SDKs: node-sdk@1.7.2, python-sdk@0.9.0. Customer routed through a corporate proxy which does TLS termination and sometimes kills idle connections. No rate-limit headers in logs.

mina: I remember a change in the streaming iterator rehydration logic landed in node-sdk 1.7.x that touched how we dedupe cached suffixes. Could be a regression where the server's prefix matching + client-side naive concat double counts. I can look at the handler that emits `last_chunk_id` vs `client_ack`.

sarah: Short term workaround: clients should dedupe by token id or rebuild output idempotently (remove trailing overlap). I'll post a small helper for both Node and Py that trims the overlapping suffix until we patch. :hammer: 

sarah: Node helper (very small):
```js
function appendTokens(buffer, tokens) {
  // naive dedupe: if last 8 chars of buffer === first 8 of tokens, drop overlap
  const overlap = 8;
  if (buffer.slice(-overlap) === tokens.slice(0, overlap)) {
    return buffer + tokens.slice(overlap);
  }
  return buffer + tokens;
}
```

kevin: Billing note: current billing counts tokens at request completion. If the service logs two separate 'end' events for a resumed stream, our metering pipeline can treat them as two billable chunks. We should make resume semantics emit a single canonical `request_id` and only finalise billing once idempotency is confirmed. Filing a billing follow-up ticket after root cause.

ryan: Can you capture raw SSE frames (client-side) and the server-side emitter logs for one of the failing sessions? Need to see whether the duplicate token is emitted twice by runtime or replayed from cache. If it's emitted once but client receives twice, that's a proxy/connection-level replay.

natalie: I got a pcap from the customer showing both frames on the wire (server->client) after reconnect. attaching excerpt: `SSE: data: {"id":"t45","token":" confirmed"}` appears twice, 3s apart.

mina: Ok that's evidence server emitted again. Two hypotheses: 1) runtime mistakenly re-sent last buffer chunk when resuming KV cache pointer, or 2) resume logic calls `flush_pending()` on reconnect which replays last buffered tokens. There's a new codepath in commit f2b9e61 (runtime streaming-warmup) that might be responsible.

ryan: Could you also include the exact SDK headers used? We added `X-Redwood-Stream-Offset` in a patch recently; if client doesn't persist it across reconnects we might default to replay.

natalie: Headers snapshot:
```
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
User-Agent: node-sdk/1.7.2
X-Redwood-Stream-Offset: 0
```

natalie: Customer didn't persist offset and on reconnect we treat offset=0 -> server sends from last confirmed boundary which may include already-sent tokens.

mina: Repro plan for me: spin local runtime with commit f2b9e61 and emulate client that drops connection then reconnects without persisting offset. See if we can replicate. If yes, patch to require server to avoid re-emitting tokens already acked unless client explicitly requests replay.

kevin: Billing mitigation: I'll add logic to metering pipeline to coalesce consecutive `end` events within a small time-window if they share request_id and same client IP. That should avoid double-charges during this window while we fix server behavior.

ryan: Nice. For triage - priority P1 for customer SLA impact. Assigning to eng-runtime + devex for a recommended SDK hotfix.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-314 (P1) - streaming-replay-duplicate-tokens. Pager alert sent to #eng-runtime and #support.

mina: Quick update: I reproduced locally by forcing `X-Redwood-Stream-Offset: 0` on reconnect and saw duplicate token emission. Root cause: runtime treats `offset` absent/zero as "replay from last checkpoint" even if server had partially flushed. Patch idea: require server to supply `stream_position` cookie and rely on that; if client omits offset treat as resume-at-current-stream-end instead of replay. Working on PR now.

sarah: Devex hotfix guidance: publish patch to node-sdk and python-sdk that (a) persists `X-Redwood-Stream-Offset` across reconnects, (b) exposes a small `dedupe_overlap_bytes` option defaulting to 0 and recommend 8-16 for corporate proxies. I'll prepare the release notes and snippets.

natalie: Customer on call is OK with workaround for now; they asked for ETA. Ryan/mina any estimate for a patch & sdk hotfix?

mina: I'll open runtime PR today and aim for canary deploy in 24-36 hours. If canary looks good we'll merge and cut a runtime patch. SDKs: small change and publish patch within 48 hours after runtime fix confirmed.

ryan: Thanks. I'll coordinate the rollout schedule and we will notify customer before canary. Please upload unit test + reproducer into the ticket so support can share.

natalie: Uploaded reproducer script and pcap to INC-2026-314. Also added a short note for support: "advise clients to persist stream offset across reconnects and apply token-dedupe helper until patch lands". :thumbsup:

mina: PR link (draft): https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4823 (fix streaming resume replay). will update status.

kevin: Billing ticket created: BILL-2026-78 to coalesce duplicate ends.

natalie: thanks all — I'll keep customer updated. Closing this thread once runtime is merged and sdk hotfix released. :pray:
